newsitem.title: FRANCE: New Airbus A330 model makes maiden flight.
newsitem.headline: New Airbus A330 model makes maiden flight.

text.p: The new Airbus A330-200 twin-jet took off on its first test flight Wednesday, carrying the European consortium's latest offensive against newly merged rival Boeing Co. in the world airline market. Airbus Industrie faces stiffer competition following last month's merger between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas Corp. to form a Goliath with annual sales of $48 billion in commercial and military aircraft and space activities.

The A330-200, launched in November 1995 and costing $450 million to develop, directly attacks the Boeing 767 family, Airbus Senior Vice President Commercial John Leahy said, after reporters watched the plane take off Wednesday morning from an Aerospatiale facility in Toulouse in southwestern France.
The four-nation Airbus consortium believes it will sell between 500 and 600 of the new planes over the next 20 years, at a catalogue price of around $110 million, Leahy said.
Airbus has already received a total of 132 orders and commitments for the A330-200 even before its first flight and "maybe we will revise upwards our estimate," Leahy said.
Airbus Vice President for Marketing Colin Stuart said the A330-200 will fly further, faster and carry more passengers and freight than Boeing's 767-300 and 767-400 aircraft.
"We are not interested in being a niche player," Stewart said. "We are intent on being on equal terms with Boeing in the marketplace."
Airbus aims to win "consistently at least 50 percent of the the market," he added. The consortium expects to hold half the world market by 2003.

The new plane allows airlines to fly non-stop, long-haul routes economically, with fewer passengers and increased cargoes. These so-called "long, thin routes," make it unprofitable to fly frequent services using larger aircraft.

Besides competing with the Boeing 767, Airbus hopes to sell the A330-200 as a replacement for the vast fleet of McDonnell Douglas DC-10s and Lockheed L-1011s in service, as well as the first generation of Airbus A300s and A310s sold since the 1970s.
The first delivery of an A330-200 is due in April 1998 to charter operator Canada 3000, which is leasing the plane from U.S. leasing company ILFC.

The A330-200 seats 253 passengers in three classes and flies up to 6,450 miles at about Mach 0.82. It is a shorter version of the basic A330-300, which seats 295 passengers in three classes and flies 7,300 miles.
